blocks.content: The National Green Tribunal is not bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by principles of natural justice.

rows: Guided by Principles of Natural Justice
Bound strictly by Code of Civil Procedure (CPC), 1908
Mandated disposal within 6 months of filing
No fixed statutory timeframe for case disposal
Judicial Members and Technical Expert Members
Members are not eligible for reappointment
Subject to standard judicial service rules

items: NGT members are NOT eligible for reappointment after their 5-year term.
Appeals against the award/decision of NGT lie directly to the Supreme Court within 90 days.
NGT jurisdiction covers 7 civil environmental laws, but explicitly EXCLUDES the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers Act, 2006.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The National Green Tribunal (NGT) was established in 2010 under the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010 for effective and speedy disposal of cases relating to environmental protection.
India became the third country in the world (and the first developing country) to establish a specialized environmental tribunal, after Australia and New Zealand.
The Tribunal is not bound by the procedure laid down under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, but is guided by principles of natural justice.
NGT is mandated to make an endeavor for final disposal of applications or appeals within 6 months of filing.
The Chairperson, Judicial Members, and Expert Members hold office for a term of 5 years and are strictly not eligible for reappointment.
